newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF confirms changing futures contracts. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MATIF confirms changing futures contracts. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]

text.p: The MATIF French futures and options exchange said on Wednesday it would change the characteristics of government bonds underlying its futures to adapt to Euro-based products.

The changes from December 1997 to the "Notionnel", the bond underlying the futures, will be a reduction in the coupon to 5.5 percent from 10 percent, a maturity of between 8.5 and 10.5 years, instead of between seven and 10 years (Corrects transposed maturities).
The nominal value will remain 500,000 francs (Corrects figure).
Earlier on Wednesday the stock market authority approved the changes.
MATIF said that in the future there must be 40 billion francs outstanding of a government bond issue for it to be eligible, instead of five billion now.
"These measures, decided after a wide consultation among the users of the contract, aim to make of the MATIF's notionnel a real 10-year product on the French rate curve," MATIF said.
It said the coupon cut made the underlying bond less expensive to deliver.
"This decision is...part of the strategy to adapt the MATIF products to the single currency and prepare the future euro rate curve," it added.
MATIF said that preparing market liquidity in 10 year franc contracts would allow to feed liquidity for the future 10-year contract on euro rates.
